Title: La Casa Blanca prevé elecciones en Venezuela en 18 o 24 meses, según 'The Wall Street Journal'

Summary: 
According to 'The Wall Street Journal', the Trump administration anticipates democratic elections in Venezuela within 18 to 24 months following the January 3, 2026, U.S. military operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The administration has not publicly specified transition timelines but has signaled that cooperation with interim President Delcy Rodríguez is temporary. The most recent presidential elections were held on July 28, 2024, in which Maduro claimed re-election despite widespread allegations of fraud; several countries, including the U.S., recognized opposition candidate Edmundo González Urrutia, backed by opposition leader María Corina Machado. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated before the Senate that the goal is a 'democratic Venezuela' through 'free and fair elections,' emphasizing that the transition will take time, not weeks. Machado, currently in exile in the U.S., has expressed her desire to return to Venezuela soon but remains skeptical about collaborating with Rodríguez, warning that the transition must be 'real' and not a 'Russian-style model' where criminal networks retain control. On January 30, 2026, U.S. Ambassador Laura Dogu arrived in Caracas to reopen the American embassy, closed for seven years after diplomatic relations were severed. Her arrival followed Rodríguez’s announcement of a general amnesty for political prisoners and the closure of the Helicoide, a notorious detention center known for human rights abuses and torture.

Title: Trump descarta eleições na Venezuela dentro de 30 dias

Summary: 
U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Monday, January 5, 2026, that there will be no elections in Venezuela within the next 30 days, following the capture of dictator Nicolás Maduro by U.S. forces on Saturday, January 3, 2026. In an interview with NBC, Trump said, 'We need to fix the country first. We can't have elections. Trump did not mention supporting Edmundo González, the winner of the 2024 fraudulent presidential election, nor did he endorse María Corina Machado as a leader, claiming she lacks sufficient domestic support and respect. Trump announced that the U.S. government may subsidize oil company projects to rebuild Venezuela’s oil infrastructure, which he estimated could be completed in less than 18 months. He stated, 'A huge amount of money will have to be spent, and the oil companies will spend it, and then they’ll be reimbursed by us or through oil revenues.' Trump confirmed that senior figures in his administration—Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, and Vice President J.D. Vance—would coordinate U.S. actions in Venezuela. He insisted that the U.S. is not at war with Caracas, but rather with drug traffickers and those responsible for sending criminals, drug addicts, and psychiatric patients to the United States, accusing Maduro of facilitating such migration during the Joe Biden administration (2021–2025).
